name: CBOR decoding (glz::read_cbor)
description:
HARNESS RULES FOR THIS GROUP: (a) the MAIN PATH below runs on every input with the full input, exactly as listed; it is the baseline, the rest of this Logic Group only adds to it. (b) Entries marked 'same core / alternative' reach the same internal code as the main call: never replace the main call with them and never run all of them on every input (fan-out kills exec/s); if used, run at most one of them as an extra step chosen by spare input bits. (c) A configuration switch must never take inputs away from the main path; options that only add code (e.g. detail/verbose output) stay ON. (d) This list is incomplete; what the project's own fuzzers, tests and examples do with the target stays in scope.
MAIN PATH (keep on every input, the whole input buffer is the CBOR payload; no selector byte stripped from it):
1. glz::read_cbor(value, buffer) into ONE rich reflected struct whose members together reach many from<CBOR,T> specializations through decode_hash_with_size key dispatch: int, double, std::string, std::array<uint64_t,N>, std::optional<std::string>, std::map<std::string,int>, std::vector<nested struct {int, std::string, std::vector<double>}>, std::variant<int,std::string,double>, std::chrono::system_clock::time_point (CBOR tag 0/1 datetime, docs/chrono.md:405) and glz::epoch_seconds. Extra member types (std::set, std::complex<double>, std::array<uint8_t,N>, a struct alternative in the variant) are added as MORE members of this struct, not as separate per-input types.
2. On success: glz::write_cbor(value, out) and glz::write_json(value, json) on the decoded value (write_json runs the JSON writer: json/write.hpp, util/zmij.hpp float formatting, itoa). On failure: glz::format_error(ec) and glz::format_error(ec, buffer) (core/reflect.hpp:3338-3359).
3. glz::read_cbor<T>(buffer) (expected<T,error_ctx> overload, same core) on the same bytes.
4. glz::read_cbor<glz::generic>(buffer): schemaless destination (glz::generic = generic_json<num_mode::f64>, include/glaze/json/generic_fwd.hpp:110-117,551; objects are ordered_small_map) decodes ANY CBOR major type (map/array/text/number/bool/null) without the early type-mismatch exit of a typed destination. On success write_json(generic) plus glz::is_array / glz::is_object; on failure format_error. Every LG harness so far dropped this and lost the generic + JSON-writer code (largest single loss).
5. Mutable buffer variant: copy the input into a std::vector<char>/std::string, append '\0', and read_cbor(struct, mutable_buffer) again (non-const resizable buffer path).
ADDITIONS on top (choose at most ONE per input from a selector derived without removing bytes, e.g. Size % N): read_cbor into std::map<std::string,std::vector<int>>, std::vector<struct>, std::vector<int64_t>, or std::variant<..., struct> (2-element [index,value] -> emplace_runtime_variant); round-trip write_cbor -> read_cbor<T>. A previous LG harness that replaced steps 1-5 by a 1-of-5 type selector lost ~18 points; one that decoded all types per input dropped exec/s 4x.

FEATURE DESCRIPTION (from the Logic Group stage):
Decodes an untrusted, attacker-controlled CBOR byte buffer into a strongly-typed C++ value (struct, container, variant, map, string/byte-string, number, chrono type, etc.) by walking a byte-at-a-time major-type/additional-info state machine (glz::cbor_detail + the from<CBOR,T> specializations). This is a classic binary-format parser attack surface: integer/length decoding, map/array/byte-string header handling, recursive-depth tracking, hashed-key field dispatch for objects, and runtime-variant selection all operate directly on adversarial bytes, so bugs here (OOB reads, integer overflow in lengths, infinite recursion, type confusion) are directly exploitable from fuzz input.
- glz::read_cbor: target; calls glz::read<opts{.format=CBOR}> which invokes the parse<CBOR>::op dispatcher that recursively calls the from<CBOR,T> specializations (the core).
- glz::read_cbor (Buffer-only overload returning expected<T,error_ctx>): variant of the target, same core, just constructs T internally instead of taking it by reference.
- glz::read_file_cbor: source/variant — reads a CBOR buffer from a file via file_to_buffer then calls the same read<set_cbor<Opts>()> path, reaching the same core; useful to additionally exercise ctx.current_file-driven error paths.
- glz::write_cbor / glz::write_file_cbor: inverse operation (encoder) of the same feature; pairing them lets the harness build round-trip (encode known value, mutate/fuzz the bytes, decode) or straight decode-of-raw-bytes tests, and the encoder's output shapes are a good seed corpus for the decoder's core.
- Input space (what adds new paths through the core from<CBOR,T> specializations, i.e. what to vary in the fuzzed byte buffer, not API flags): the CBOR major type byte (map=5, array=4, tstr=3, bstr=2, uint=0, negint=1, tag=6, simple/float=7), additional-info sub-byte (direct value 0-23, 24/25/26/27 = uint8/16/32/64-follows length, 31 = indefinite-length with break-code 0xFF terminator), semantic tags (0/1 = datetime string/epoch, 4 = decimal fraction, 43000 = complex number, typed-array tags per RFC 8746 with endianness-swap paths), nested/indefinite maps and arrays to drive recursion up to max_recursive_depth_limit, variant encoding as a 2-element [index, value] array to exercise emplace_runtime_variant and no_matching_variant_type, and object field keys (tstr) whose length and hash drive decode_hash_with_size field dispatch versus unknown-key skip_value<CBOR> paths. The target type T chosen by the harness (struct with reflect<T>::size>0, readable_map_t, readable_array_t, is_variant, chrono/time_point wrappers, byte-string/std::array<byte,N>) also selects which from<CBOR,T> core routines run, so varying T is the most impactful "mode" dimension.
This list is incomplete; what the project's own fuzzers and tests do with the target stays.
